import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class I {
    
    public static boolean DEBUG = true;
    public static String name = "I";

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        FastScanner scan;
        PrintWriter out;
        if (DEBUG) {
            scan = new FastScanner(System.in);
            out = new PrintWriter(System.out);
        } else {
            scan = new FastScanner(name + ".in");
            out = new PrintWriter(new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(name + ".out")));
        }

        int N = Integer.parseInt(scan.nextString());
        double P = Double.parseDouble(scan.nextString());
        
        int i = 0;
        for(; i<=N; i+=1) {
            double favorable = 0;
            
            // Case 1: Johnny studies i maps
            // We need to count scenarios where at least one of the studied maps is selected
            
            // Total ways to choose 3 maps from N
            double total = (double)N * (N-1) * (N-2) / 6.0;
            
            // Count favorable cases:
            // Case 1: All 3 maps are studied -> Johnny can pick any, system picks randomly among remaining 2
            // Case 2: 2 maps studied, 1 not studied -> Johnny will pick the unstudied one, system picks from 2 studied
            // Case 3: 1 map studied, 2 not studied -> Johnny picks one of the unstudied, system picks from 2 unstudied (might be studied or not)
            // Case 4: 0 maps studied -> system picks randomly from 3 unstudied
            
            // Better approach: Count cases where NO studied map is played
            // Then favorable = total - cases_with_no_studied_map
            
            double noStudied = 0;
            if (N - i >= 3) {
                noStudied = (double)(N-i) * (N-i-1) * (N-i-2) / 6.0;
            }
            
            // Cases where exactly 2 unstudied and 1 studied:
            // System must pick the studied map only if both players discard the unstudied ones
            // Each player picks one to discard; if both pick unstudied, system picks from remaining (1 unstudied + 1 studied)
            // For studied map to NOT be played: both players must discard the studied map (impossible if only 1 studied) or system picks unstudied
            // Actually, let's recalculate directly for favorable cases
            
            // Direct calculation of favorable cases:
            // Case A: 3 studied maps selected
            //   Johnny can discard any of the 3 studied maps
            //   System randomly picks from remaining 2 studied maps
            //   Probability studied map is played = 1 (since all 3 are studied)
            if (i >= 3) {
                favorable += (double)i * (i-1) * (i-2) / 6.0;
            }
            
            // Case B: 2 studied, 1 unstudied
            //   Johnny wants to avoid unstudied, so he discards unstudied
            //   Opponent discards randomly among 3
            //   If opponent discards unstudied: system picks from 2 studied -> studied played
            //   If opponent discards studied: system picks from {1 studied, 1 unstudied} -> 50% chance studied
            //   If opponent discards other studied: same as above
            //   Actually: Johnny discards unstudied. Opponent randomly discards one of 3.
            //   - Opponent discards unstudied (prob 1/3): system picks from 2 studied -> studied played
            //   - Opponent discards studied (prob 2/3): system picks from {1 studied, 1 unstudied} -> 50% chance
            //   So probability = 1/3 * 1 + 2/3 * 1/2 = 2/3
            if (i >= 2 && N - i >= 1) {
                favorable += (double)i * (i-1) / 2 * (N-i) * (2.0/3.0);
            }
            
            // Case C: 1 studied, 2 unstudied
            //   Johnny wants to avoid unstudied, so he discards one unstudied
            //   Opponent randomly discards one of 3
            //   Johnny discards unstudied. Opponent:
            //   - Discards studied (1/3): system picks from {1 unstudied, 1 unstudied} -> unstudied played
            //   - Discards unstudied (2/3): system picks from {1 studied, 1 unstudied} -> 50% chance studied
            //   So probability = 2/3 * 1/2 = 1/3
            if (i >= 1 && N - i >= 2) {
                favorable += (double)i * (N-i) * (N-i-1) / 2 * (1.0/3.0);
            }
            
            // Case D: 0 studied, 3 unstudied
            //   Probability studied played = 0
            //   (already handled by noStudied)
            
            double prob = favorable / total;
            
            if(prob >= P) {
                break;
            }
        }
        
        out.println(i);

        out.close();
    }

    static class FastScanner {
        InputStream dis;
        byte[] buffer = new byte[1 << 17];
        int pointer = 0;

        public FastScanner (String fileName) throws IOException {
            dis = new FileInputStream(fileName);
        }

        public FastScanner (InputStream is) throws IOException {
            dis = is;
        }

        int nextInt() throws IOException {
            int ret = 0;

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            boolean negative = false;
            if (b == '-') {
                negative = true;
                b = nextByte();
            }
            while (b >= '0' && b <= '9') {
                ret = 10 * ret + b - '0';
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return (negative) ? -ret : ret;
        }

        long nextLong() throws IOException {
            long ret = 0;

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            boolean negative = false;
            if (b == '-') {
                negative = true;
                b = nextByte();
            }
            while (b >= '0' && b <= '9') {
                ret = 10 * ret + b - '0';
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return (negative) ? -ret : ret;
        }

        byte nextByte() throws IOException {
            if (pointer == buffer.length) {
                dis.read(buffer, 0, buffer.length);
                pointer = 0;
            }
            return buffer[pointer++];
        }

        String nextString() throws IOException {
            StringBuilder ret = new StringBuilder();

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            while (b > ' ') {
                ret.appendCodePoint(b);
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return ret.toString();
        }

    }
}
